beads.title: signal4s 1.0 — compact calculus of sampled signals
beads.body:
Umbrella epic for signal4s before 1.0.

Spine: Signal + Kernel + System Representation + Plan + Runner + Typed Result Axes.

Not a SciPy/gsignal port. SciPy is evidence via versioned fixtures; API contracts come from proposal.md.

## Exit criteria (1.0)
- All child epics E0–E10 closed
- Required scope in proposal.md §6 implemented
- Law suite green on JVM + Scala.js for core/fft/design/laws
- SciPy fixture parity suite green for every required numerical path
- Explicit supported/unsupported matrix published

## Source
proposal.md (2026-07-31)

beads.title: E0: SciPy / gsignal versioned fixture harness
beads.body:
Offline fixture generator + committed golden vectors. No Python/R at test runtime.

## Goal
Produce versioned JSON/NPY-style fixtures from pinned SciPy (and optionally gsignal) that Scala tests load as evidence.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `fixtures/` layout documented (schema, SciPy version, gsignal version if used, generation command)
- [ ] Generator script pinned to exact SciPy version; output is deterministic
- [ ] Fixtures committed; CI/tests do not invoke Python
- [ ] Each fixture records: operation name, inputs, parameters, expected outputs, rtol/atol, SciPy API used
- [ ] Coverage catalog maps each required 1.0 numerical path → fixture ids
- [ ] Impulse, step, on-bin / between-bin sinusoids, even/odd kernels, short signals included as base set

## SciPy checks (this epic *is* the harness)
- Pin and record `scipy.__version__` (and numpy) in fixture metadata
- Prefer stable SciPy APIs: `convolve`, `correlate`, `lfilter`, `sosfilt`, `filtfilt`, `firwin`, `butter`, `sosfreqz`, `stft`/`ShortTimeFFT`, `welch`, `resample_poly` / `upfirdn`, `fft`/`rfft`
- Document known semantic mismatches (e.g. mode=same vs Kernel origin) so fixtures test *numeric* agreement under an explicit mapping, not blind API cloning

beads.title: E1: Foundation — build, axes, Signal, Kernel, errors
beads.body:
Cross-project build + core ontology. No convolution yet.

## Goal
signal4s-core and signal4s-laws exist; SampleRate/Frequency/Sampling/Signal/Kernel/SignalError are precise and tested.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] sbt multi-project: core + laws; JVM + Scala.js cross for both
- [ ] Gale is a real dependency of core
- [ ] Smart constructors return Either[SignalError, _]; `.orThrow` for tests/examples
- [ ] SampleRate / Frequency reject non-positive / non-finite values
- [ ] Frequency↔rad/sample and cycles/sample require explicit SampleRate
- [ ] Kernel.causal / Kernel.at / Kernel.centeredOdd; even-length silent centering impossible
- [ ] Kernel.minLag/maxLag agree with origin + tap count (law)
- [ ] Signal carries Sampling; length from samples
- [ ] Executable doc skeleton (mdoc or equivalent placeholder)
- [ ] proposal.md linked from README stub

## SciPy checks
- None required for numeric parity yet
- Document mapping notes: SciPy arrays are bare; Signal/Kernel axes are the intentional delta

beads.title: E2: Direct convolution, boundaries, correlation, axes
beads.body:
Semantically exact convolution regions + scalar reference implementation.

## Goal
Direct convolution and correlation with explicit Boundary, OutputRegion, Kernel origin, and lag/time axes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Scalar reference direct convolution (visible, used as oracle for later optimized paths)
- [ ] OutputRegion: Full, Valid, Input(boundary)
- [ ] Boundary: Zero, Reflect at minimum; Constant/Clamp/Symmetric as designed
- [ ] Signal-axis propagation: t_out = t_in - zeroLagIndex/fs
- [ ] Correlation returns values + LagAxis; documented r_xy[ℓ]=∑ x[n] y[n+ℓ]
- [ ] Normalization enum (raw/biased/unbiased/coefficient), not Boolean
- [ ] Laws: delta identity, linearity, full commutativity (tol), length/axis laws
- [ ] Exhaustive small-vector tests
- [ ] Circular convolution is a *separate* API (not a Boundary case)

## SciPy checks
- [ ] Full zero-extension vs `scipy.signal.convolve(..., mode='full')` with causal kernels
- [ ] Valid vs `mode='valid'`
- [ ] Input(Zero) vs SciPy `mode='same'` under an *explicit* origin mapping fixture (document mapping)
- [ ] Correlation vs `scipy.signal.correlate` for same convention mapping + lag axis fixture
- [ ] Autocorrelation of impulse/sinusoid fixtures
- [ ] Even/odd kernels and nonzero origins covered by fixtures

beads.title: E3: Gale ConvolutionOperator with adjoint
beads.body:
Finite batch convolution as DoubleLinearOperator. No FFT yet.

## Goal
Zero-boundary convolution operator with proven adjoint for inverse/LS/matched-filter path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Convolution.operator(kernel, inputLength, region) for zero-extension regions
- [ ] Forward matches direct convolution reference
- [ ] Adjoint property ⟨Ax,y⟩ ≈ ⟨x,A*y⟩ with scale-aware tolerance (law)
- [ ] Reflective/clamped adjoints not advertised until implemented+tested
- [ ] Direct-kernel benchmarks (allocation + throughput) recorded
- [ ] Streaming runners do NOT extend DoubleLinearOperator (doc + API review)

## SciPy checks
- [ ] Forward operator output matches SciPy convolve fixtures (same as E2)
- [ ] Adjoint checked against explicit matrix form on small N (SciPy or dense Gale), not against a SciPy adjoint API
- [ ] Fixture: small Toeplitz / convolution matrix vs operator matvec

beads.title: E4: FIR + SOS runners, state, zero-phase
beads.body:
Immutable filter descriptions; single-owner runners; DF-II transposed SOS.

## Goal
FIR and SecondOrderCascade execution with explicit state, batch/chunk laws, and separate zero-phase path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fir(kernel); runner process / processInto / reset / snapshot
- [ ] FIR from-rest batch ≡ convolution (law)
- [ ] Biquad named coeffs with a0=1; SecondOrderCascade
- [ ] DF-II transposed implementation
- [ ] Chunking law: run(x++y,s0) ≈ run(y,s_x)
- [ ] Snapshot/restart law; two runners from one description have independent state
- [ ] DigitalTransferFunction filtering for low-order/interop
- [ ] ZeroPhase.filter as separate offline API (not runner flag); edge policy explicit
- [ ] High-order numerical stress fixtures
- [ ] Document: not thread-safe; latency; state shape; flush if any

## SciPy checks
- [ ] FIR runner vs `lfilter` / convolve mapping for causal FIR
- [ ] SOS vs `scipy.signal.sosfilt` on shared SOS coefficient fixtures
- [ ] Initial/final conditions vs SciPy zi/zf mapping fixtures
- [ ] Zero-phase vs `filtfilt` with documented padtype/edge mapping (Gustafsson etc.)
- [ ] Poles near unit circle stress cases from SciPy-generated SOS

beads.title: E5: FFT substrate — ComplexVector, plans, workspaces
beads.body:
Portable pure-Scala FFT with explicit normalization and split-complex storage.

## Goal
Immutable RealFftPlan / complex plans + single-owner workspaces; JVM and Scala.js parity.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Complex + ComplexVector(real,imag) split storage
- [ ] FftNormalization: Backward / Forward / Orthonormal
- [ ] Mixed-radix + Bluestein for arbitrary lengths
- [ ] Real↔half-complex transforms
- [ ] Plan immutable/thread-safe; workspace owns scratch (not cached in plan)
- [ ] forwardInto / inverseInto destination APIs
- [ ] Laws: round-trip; Parseval per normalization; real conjugate symmetry
- [ ] Spectra carry FrequencyAxis + sourceLength + normalization
- [ ] JVM + Scala.js benchmarks for common lengths

## SciPy checks
- [ ] fft/ifft vs `numpy.fft` / `scipy.fft` under each normalization mapping
- [ ] rfft/irfft half-complex layout fixtures (document packing vs SciPy)
- [ ] Non-power-of-two lengths including primes (Bluestein path)
- [ ] On-bin and between-bin sinusoid amplitude/phase fixtures

beads.title: E6: Planned FFT / overlap-add convolution + Auto
beads.body:
Meaning vs method: plans select algorithm; results match direct reference.

## Goal
FFT convolution, overlap-add, reusable ConvolutionPlan, measured Auto dispatch.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ConvolutionPlan exposes selected algorithm; reuses transformed kernel
- [ ] Direct ≡ FFT ≡ OLA within scale-aware tolerance (law)
- [ ] Circular convolution theorem law vs FFT path
- [ ] Auto dispatch driven by measured models (no folklore 256-tap rule)
- [ ] Benchmark matrix: lengths, one-shot vs reused kernel, regions, cold vs warm
- [ ] Ownership: immutable results stable after workspace reuse

## SciPy checks
- [ ] FFT/OLA outputs match SciPy convolve fixtures (same cases as E2)
- [ ] Circular conv vs `scipy.fft` product of DFTs / `convolve(..., method=)` where applicable
- [ ] Large length stress fixtures vs SciPy

beads.title: E7: Windows, framing, STFT, periodogram, Welch
beads.body:
Windows with convention; shared FramePlan; StftPlan with dual; typed spectra.

## Goal
STFT analyze/synthesize + Welch/periodogram without reimplementing framing/FFT/scaling ad hoc.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] WindowSpec + WindowConvention (Symmetric|Periodic) always required
- [ ] Window carries coherent gain, power gain, ENBW
- [ ] FramePlan reused by STFT/Welch
- [ ] StftPlan validates invertibility; CanonicalDual computed once
- [ ] TimeFrequency named axes; spectrogram derived from STFT
- [ ] Periodogram + WelchPlan (detrend/sides/scaling/average enums)
- [ ] WelchResult retains diagnostics; DoF not fabricated naively
- [ ] Laws: STFT round-trip for valid dual; axes match plan

## SciPy checks
- [ ] Periodic/symmetric Hann/Hamming/Blackman/Kaiser vs SciPy windows
- [ ] STFT vs `ShortTimeFFT` / `stft` under documented hop/window/fft mapping
- [ ] Exact inverse STFT round-trip fixtures (edge frames included)
- [ ] Welch/periodogram vs `scipy.signal.welch` / `periodogram` for scaling='spectrum'|'density', onesided
- [ ] Detrend mean/linear fixtures

beads.title: E8: FIR design + Butterworth IIR → SOS
beads.body:
Specification-driven design with physical frequency types and design reports.

## Goal
Windowed-sinc FIR + Butterworth analog→bilinear→ZPK→SOS with diagnostics.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No bare cutoff Double; Frequency + SampleRate required
- [ ] Reject frequencies above Nyquist
- [ ] FirDesign low/high/band + Kaiser order estimation
- [ ] Butterworth lowPass (and family transforms as scoped)
- [ ] Named conversions: Bilinear.transform, Sos.fromZerosPolesGain, …
- [ ] DesignedIir(zpk, sos, report); SOS primary for execution
- [ ] IirDesignReport: orders, freqs, pole magnitude, stable, warnings
- [ ] Laws: ZPK/SOS/TF responses agree after conversion; freq/impulse/step response; group delay

## SciPy checks
- [ ] firwin / firwin2 style fixtures under explicit window + fs mapping
- [ ] butter + tf2sos / zpk2sos fixtures (pairing differences documented if any)
- [ ] freqz/sosfreqz magnitude & phase fixtures
- [ ] impulse/step response fixtures
- [ ] High-order TF vs SOS conditioning warning cases

beads.title: E9: Polyphase upfirdn + rational resampling
beads.body:
One substrate for rate change; streaming contract separate from simple filter runners.

## Goal
RateRatio + polyphase resampler; decimate/resample compile to upfirdn.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] RateRatio always GCD-reduced, positive
- [ ] Polyphase decomposition of prototype FIR
- [ ] upfirdn + rational resampler expose rates, phase, delay, consume/produce, flush
- [ ] Laws: ratio reduction preserves meaning; identity ratio ≡ identity ± documented delay
- [ ] Chunk/latency laws for streaming resampler
- [ ] Conveniences do not fork independent numeric cores

## SciPy checks
- [ ] upfirdn vs `scipy.signal.upfirdn`
- [ ] resample_poly vs SciPy for several up/down pairs and phases
- [ ] Identity ratio and pure decimate/interpolate fixtures
- [ ] Edge/flush behavior documented relative to SciPy

beads.title: E10: Ravel adapters + 1.0 API/numerical audit
beads.body:
Optional N-D integration and release gate.

## Goal
signal4s-ravel for axis-wise ops; complete audit before 1.0.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Transform-along-axis and batched channel helpers (optional module)
- [ ] Contiguous copies controlled/explicit
- [ ] Core 1-D types do not depend on Ravel
- [ ] Full API audit vs proposal required/deferred lists
- [ ] Benchmark receipts attached for Auto dispatch + FFT + SOS
- [ ] Migration examples from SciPy and gsignal (docs)
- [ ] Supported/unsupported matrix published
- [ ] All SciPy fixture catalog entries green on JVM; Scala.js where applicable

## SciPy checks
- [ ] End-to-end workflow fixture: generate → filter → STFT → Welch matches SciPy pipeline under mapping doc
- [ ] Fixture catalog coverage = 100% of required §6 numerical features
- [ ] Explicit list of intentional semantic differences (Kernel origin, OutputRegion.Input, typed frequencies)
